issue.title: Closing a follow-up epic never cascades to (or relaunches the land agent of) its parent plan, so zombie epics accumulate
issue.description: close_one_and_delegated_parent in sase-core cascades a close from a plan bead to its parent only when the parent is a phase. When the parent is a plan (the epic that spawned a follow-up epic), closing the child does not cascade; the bd/land_epic instruction leaves the ancestor walk to the child's land-agent LLM. When that continuation is lost (see sase-12r) or skipped, the parent epic stays in_progress forever. Roughly 29 plan beads are currently in_progress with every child closed (e.g. sase-zu: 7 phases + 1 child epic all closed, epic still open), inside 153 in-progress beads that bury the real stalls. Fix direction per the two overnight-stall reports: rather than a blind plan-to-plan cascade, make the invariant host-owned - a liveness check that relaunches the parent plan's land agent when all children are closed and no land agent is live (belongs in sase-core per the rust-core-boundary rule), plus a one-time report-only pass to triage the existing zombies.

task_type_fields.impact: ~29 zombie epics hide real stalls and hold dependents; fleet bead status is unreadable at 153 in-progress beads
task_type_fields.location: sase-core crates/sase_core/src/bead/mutation.rs close_one_and_delegated_parent; src/sase/default_config.yml bd/land_epic ancestor-walk instruction
task_type_fields.repro: Close a follow-up epic whose parent is a plan bead without the land agent completing its ancestor walk; parent stays in_progress (current live example: sase-zu, all children closed, epic open 5d)
